target_clause: For example, if a client's signature key is compromised, it should not be possible to impersonate arbitrary servers to that client in subsequent handshakes.

Servers SHOULD send a GOAWAY frame when the closing of a connection is known in advance, even if the advance notice is small, so that the remote peer can know whether a request has been partially processed or not.

When either endpoint chooses to close the transport-layer TCP connection, the terminating endpoint SHOULD first send a GOAWAY ([GOAWAY]) frame so that both endpoints can reliably determine whether previously sent frames have been processed and gracefully complete or terminate any necessary remaining tasks.
Implementations SHOULD track the use of these features and set limits on their use.

A sender SHOULD NOT consider itself application limited if it would have fully utilized the congestion window without pacing delay.
Out-of-order packets SHOULD be acknowledged more quickly, in order to accelerate loss recovery.
A packet sent when an RTO alarm fires MAY carry new data if available or unacknowledged data to potentially reduce recovery time.
In order to accelerate loss recovery and reduce timeouts, the receiver SHOULD send an immediate ACK after it receives an out-of-order packet.

Implementers MAY experiment with using other reordering thresholds, including absolute thresholds, bearing in mind that a lower multiplier reduces reordering resilience and increases spurious retransmissions, and a higher multiplier increases loss detection delay.

It is RECOMMENDED that implementations place limits on the total lifetime of such keying material; these limits should take into account the lifetime of the peer's certificate, the likelihood of intervening revocation, and the time since the peer's online CertificateVerify signature.
The most specific reason that the cache is aware of SHOULD be used, to the extent that it is possible to implement.
Logged or otherwise persistently stored debug data MUST have adequate safeguards to prevent unauthorized access.

Clients SHOULD NOT wait indefinitely for SETTINGS to arrive before sending requests, but SHOULD process received datagrams in order to increase the likelihood of processing SETTINGS before sending the first request.
A server SHOULD avoid reusing a Push ID over a long period.
When possible, it is RECOMMENDED that servers send an HTTP response with an appropriate status code rather than canceling a request it has already begun processing.
While there are legitimate uses for some redundant packets, implementations SHOULD track redundant packets and treat excessive volumes of any non-productive packets as indicative of an attack.
Implementations SHOULD use caution in relying on any data which is contained in Initial packets that is not otherwise authenticated.

If there are unacknowledged retransmittable packets still pending, they should be marked as lost. To compensate for the reduced reordering resilience, the sender SHOULD set an alarm for a small period of time.

ACK frames SHOULD always acknowledge the most recently received packets, and the more out-of-order the packets are, the more important it is to send an updated ACK frame quickly, to prevent the peer from declaring a packet as lost and spuriusly retransmitting the frames it contains.
All implementations MUST be capable of receiving and minimally processing frames up to 214 octets in length, plus the 9-octet frame header.
Values outside this range MUST be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
An endpoint that receives an unexpected stream identifier MUST respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
Endpoints SHOULD send a GOAWAY frame when ending a connection, providing that circumstances permit it.
The value advertised by an endpoint MUST be between this initial value and the maximum allowed frame size (224-1 or 16,777,215 octets), inclusive.
Any data received after a closure alert is ignored.
Values greater than 214 (16,384) MUST NOT be sent unless the receiver has set a larger value for SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
If the scheme does not have a mandatory authority component and none is provided in the request target, the request MUST NOT contain the ":authority" pseudo-header and "Host" header fields.
SETTINGS frames always apply to a connection, never a single stream, and MUST only be sent on the connection control stream (Stream 3).
In order to provide such synchronization timepoints, the recipient of a SETTINGS frame in which the ACK flag is not set MUST apply the updated parameters as soon as possible upon receipt.
